add_btn.what: Adds a row with a guide field, a position target, an aim target and its axes. Each field has a << button to fill it from the selection.
examples: Click +, fill the elbow guide and the vertex it should sit on.
Add one row per finger knuckle to place a hand from vertices.

place_guide_btn.what: Moves every guide in the list to its target position.
steps: Check the aims on elbows and knees.
examples: After loading a new model, click it to snap all guides to their spots.
Place the guides again after the model changed proportions.
place_guide_btn.details: For each row: moves the guide to the target position (a cluster on the components if they are vertices), then aims it with the aim / up axes. One undo chunk.

create_ik_refs_btn.what: Makes reference planes from the start / mid / end guides of each row, used to keep IK chains flat.
examples: Fill shoulder / elbow / wrist and click it to see the arm plane.
Check the leg guides are flat before building the knee.
create_ik_refs_btn.details: Builds a reference plane through start / mid / end so the mid guide stays on the chain plane.

add_ref_btn.what: Adds a new start / mid / end row for one more IK chain.
examples: Click + once per limb: arms and legs.
Add a row for the tail if you rig it with IK.
add_ref_btn.details: Adds start / mid / end fields, each with a << button that copies the selection.

run_btn.tip: Run the code in the field.
run_btn.what: Runs the Python or MEL code typed in the field (pick the language above).
examples: Paste a small script that moves extra guides and click Run.
Snap custom extra guides after Place Guides.
run_btn.details: exec() for Python or mel.eval for MEL, inside one undo chunk.
